item.title: LOT-105: smiley search, history and wiki keywords
item.body:
LOT-105
Closes #196
Claim: cloud/lot-105

**Problem.** The smiley picker (LOT-104) has no search, no history and no keywords; legacy `CombinedSmileyPickerView` has all three, and adding a favourite from the UI went through them.

**Change.** Search bar in the picker sheet ("Rechercher", "Tous les mots clés", legacy `@AppStorage` key), results grid (tap opens the detail), history chips (recent / frequent, 5), wiki keywords in the detail (tap = search). `SmileySearchModel` (`@Observable @MainActor`) over LOT-053's `SmileyLookupFlow` and LOT-064's `SmileySearchHistoryStore`; no engine or network change. Only the latest request counts (generation guard). The search model lives as long as the reply sheet (legacy session state). A text under 3 characters says why; a failed search is not shown as "no result" (LESSONS 44); a code served twice is listed once. Spec: `docs/lots/LOT-105-smiley-search.md`; CHANGELOG-LEGACY row 74.

**Tests.** `SmileySearchModelTests` (Swift Testing, gated fake lookups, no clock). Not built locally (cloud): CI "App build + tests" is the check. SwiftLint `--strict` clean locally. Adversarial review by Opus: round 1 REQUEST CHANGES (missing import, a test racing the task, search state lost on reopen, weak chips test), fixed; round 2 APPROVE (minor findings fixed).

**Pending capture** (LOT-053 list, #360): see the spec; nothing hand-built.

## Mac check needed
For `mac/m2-lead`:
- [ ] Reply sheet → Smileys: search bar at the bottom, iPhone and iPad; keyboard "Rechercher" key submits.
- [ ] Type 1-2 characters: hint "Saisissez au moins 3 caractères…", button disabled. 3+: results grid.
- [ ] "chat", then "chat noir" with and without "Tous les mots clés" (the toggle survives reopening): results sane; no smiley shown twice.
- [ ] A nonsense word → "Aucun smiley trouvé"; airplane mode → "Recherche impossible", back button returns to the catalogue.
- [ ] Tap a result → detail: Insérer, Ajouter aux favoris (notice at the top, then it shows in "Favoris de l’app"), "Mots clés" chips load; tap a keyword → detail closes and it is searched.
- [ ] Insert a result, reopen the panel: same text and results (legacy behaviour).
- [ ] History chips: after a search with results, reopen: chip shown (clock icon); typing filters (magnifier icon); tap runs the search; max 5.
- [ ] Logged out: no search bar, no crash.
- [ ] Light, dark, Dynamic Type XL (bar, chips, detail with keywords).

comments.body:
Walkthrough

The composer now provides smiley lookup and search-history services to the picker. The picker supports smiley searches, suggestions, and wiki keywords, with search state retained across picker presentations. **Changes: Smiley Search and Keywords** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Lookup and history services**
`App/SwiftHFR/Smileys/SmileyLookups.swift`, `App/SwiftHFR/Composer/ReplyPosting.swift`, `App/SwiftHFR/Composer/ReplyComposerModel.swift`, `App/SwiftHFR/Composer/ReplyComposerView.swift`|Composer services provide live smiley lookups and a shared, persisted search-history store. The composer passes panel services to the picker and retains its search model across picker presentations.| |**Search and keyword state**
`App/SwiftHFR/Smileys/SmileySearchModel.swift`, `App/SwiftHFRTests/Smileys/SmileySearchModelTests.swift`, `docs/CHANGELOG-LEGACY.md`|`SmileySearchModel` handles trimmed search input, result deduplication, history, suggestions, wiki keywords, and stale requests. Tests cover these states and behaviors. The legacy changelog describes short-input, failure, and duplicate-result behavior.| |**Picker search and keyword experience**
`App/SwiftHFR/Smileys/SmileyPickerModel.swift`, `App/SwiftHFR/Smileys/SmileyPickerView.swift`, `App/SwiftHFRTests/Smileys/SmileySearchModelTests.swift`, `docs/lots/LOT-104-smiley-picker.md`, `docs/lots/LOT-105-smiley-search.md`|The picker presents search results, suggestions, and keyword states. Users can open a result’s detail and submit keyword searches. The LOT-104 and LOT-105 documents describe the picker and search behavior.| **Estimated code review effort:** 3 (Moderate) | ~25 minutes **Change:** Feature ### Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant SmileyPickerView participant SmileySearchModel participant SmileyLookups participant SearchHistoryStore SmileyPickerView->>SmileySearchModel: Submit search text and matching mode SmileySearchModel->>SmileyLookups: Search with trimmed text and matching mode SmileyLookups-->>SmileySearchModel: Return smiley results SmileySearchModel->>SearchHistoryStore: Record search with results SmileySearchModel-->>SmileyPickerView: Publish search state ``` **Possibly related issues** - ezzz/HFRnow#461: The issue requests a forum-favourites section with smiley details and an app-favourite action. This PR supports opening a search result’s detail, where the favourite action is available, but does not add the requested section. **Possibly related PRs** - [ezzz/HFRnow#459](https://github.com/ezzz/HFRnow/pull/459): Adds the smiley picker and detail view that this PR extends with search, history, and keyword searches.
Merge Risk: Minimal · up to 54308

The smiley search, history and keyword feature has no remaining concrete defects in the supplied review. The earlier concern about a misnamed test has been addressed, so the change looks ready to merge once CI passes.
Security architecture risk: Low · up to 54308

The change has a bounded client-side scope and reuses existing request and storage controls. Search history is intentionally shared across accounts on the device. No material security regression was established, but account-change behavior and on-device dismissal behavior were not fully verified. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details

**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The reviewed flow affects the current account's lookup requests, local device history, and user-selected favorites. No new administrative or cross-service authority was identified in this wiring; history visibility nevertheless spans accounts using the same application data on the device. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The search flow obtains account cookies and uses a separate probe transport; wiki lookups use the anonymous transport. Wiki responses must identify the requested smiley code before their keywords are accepted. - _observed_ — Remote search HTML is parsed into smiley data rather than rendered as executable HTML. Image URLs pass through the HTTP/HTTPS URL helper, then the existing native thumbnail loader, which requests images with allowsThirdParty set to false. This integration does not substitute the authenticated lookup transport for image loading. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — Lookup failures remain distinct from empty results. History recording rejects zero-result searches, and a refused history write does not hide already published results. The storage core refuses mutations after failed loads and publishes updated memory only after persistence succeeds, containing storage failure without overwriting unreadable history.

+import Foundation
+import HFRClient
+import HFRModels
+import HFRNetwork
+import HFRParsing
+import HFRStorage
+import Observation
+
+// Port of HFRswift/Swift/AnswerView.swift (CombinedSmileyPickerView search: performSearch, suggestionChips, FavoriteSmileyDetailView
+// keywords) @ 2440d79. Differences: a failed search says so instead of "Aucun smiley trouvé" (LESSONS 44); a text under 3
+// characters explains itself; results are listed once per code (GAP-088).
+/// State of the smiley search of the picker (LOT-105): the text, the results, the history chips and the wiki keywords.
+///
+/// Port of the search half of legacy's `CombinedSmileyPickerView` (`AnswerView.swift:1230-1345` @ 2440d79) over LOT-053's
+/// `SmileyLookupFlow` and LOT-064's `SmileySearchHistoryStore`. Only the latest request counts: an older answer that
+/// arrives after a newer search, a clear or a closed panel is dropped.
+@MainActor
+@Observable
+final class SmileySearchModel {
+    /// What the results area shows.
+    enum Phase: Equatable {
+        /// The catalogue (no search made, or the search was cleared).
+        case library
+        /// A request is in flight.
+        case loading
+        /// Smileys found, once per code, in the order served.
+        case results([PickerSmiley])
+        /// HFR found nothing (its own "no result" answer).
+        case empty
+        /// The text is under the minimum length; nothing was sent.
+        case tooShort
+        /// The search could not be made or read; the text tells why.
+        case failed(String)
+    }
+
+    /// What the wiki keywords of the open detail show.
+    enum Keywords: Equatable {
+        /// Nothing asked yet.
+        case idle
+        /// The request is in flight.
+        case loading
+        /// The keywords of the wiki entry, in the order served (empty: the entry has none).
+        case loaded([String])
+        /// The entry could not be read; the text tells why.
+        case failed(String)
+    }
+
+    /// The shortest search HFR is asked for, in characters (legacy `SmileySearchService.swift:19`).
+    static let minimumLength = HFREndpoint.smileySearchMinimumLength
+    /// The suggestions shown at most (legacy `suggestionChips`, `AnswerView.swift:1088-1093`).
+    static let suggestionLimit = 5
+
+    /// The search field; the view calls `refreshSuggestions()` when it changes.
+    var text = ""
+    private(set) var phase = Phase.library
+    private(set) var keywords = Keywords.idle
+    /// The history chips: the recent searches first, then the most frequent ones, matching `text`.
+    private(set) var suggestions: [SmileySearchHistoryEntry] = []
+
+    private let lookups: any SmileyLookups
+    private let history: SmileySearchHistoryStore
+    private var generation = 0
+    private var keywordsGeneration = 0
+    private var searchTask: Task<Void, Never>?
+
+    /// A search model over the forum lookups and the device's history.
+    init(lookups: any SmileyLookups, history: SmileySearchHistoryStore) {
+        self.lookups = lookups
+        self.history = history
+    }
+
+    /// The search can be sent: at least `minimumLength` characters once trimmed.
+    var canSearch: Bool { trimmed.count >= Self.minimumLength }
+
+    /// Why a typed text cannot be searched yet; nil when it can, or when the field is empty.
+    var tooShortHint: String? {
+        guard !trimmed.isEmpty, !canSearch else { return nil }
+        return "Saisissez au moins \(Self.minimumLength) caractères pour lancer une recherche."
+    }
+
+    /// Whether the results area replaces the catalogue.
+    var isSearching: Bool { phase != .library }
+
+    private var trimmed: String { text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }
+
+    // MARK: Search
+
+    /// Starts a search for `query` (the field's text when nil), replacing the one in flight.
+    func submit(_ query: String? = nil, requireAll: Bool) {
+        // The field shows the text at once, not when the task starts.
+        if let query, query != text { text = query }
+        searchTask?.cancel()
+        searchTask = Task { await search(query, requireAll: requireAll) }
+    }
+
+    /// Searches `query` (the field's text when nil) and shows the outcome; a successful search is remembered.
+    func search(_ query: String? = nil, requireAll: Bool) async {
+        if let query, query != text { text = query }
+        // A request cancelled before it started must not touch the phase.
+        guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
+        let query = trimmed
+        generation += 1
+        let mine = generation
+        guard query.count >= Self.minimumLength else {
+            phase = .tooShort
+            return
+        }
+        phase = .loading
+        let found: [ForumSmiley]
+        do throws(SmileyLookupError) {
+            found = try await lookups.search(query, requireAll: requireAll)
+        } catch {
+            guard mine == generation, !Task.isCancelled else { return }
+            phase = .failed(Self.message(for: error))
+            return
+        }
+        guard mine == generation, !Task.isCancelled else { return }
+        let smileys = Self.listed(found)
+        phase = smileys.isEmpty ? .empty : .results(smileys)
+        // The history is a convenience: a store that refuses the write must not hide the results.
+        _ = try? await history.record(query, resultCount: smileys.count)
+        await refreshSuggestions()
+    }
+
+    /// Back to the catalogue; a search in flight is dropped.
+    func clear() {
+        searchTask?.cancel()
+        generation += 1
+        phase = .library
+    }
+
+    /// Drops everything in flight when the panel closes; a search dropped while loading goes back to the catalogue, so the
+    /// reopened panel never waits for an answer that will not come.
+    func stop() {
+        searchTask?.cancel()
+        generation += 1
+        keywordsGeneration += 1
+        if phase == .loading { phase = .library }
+    }
+
+    // MARK: History
+
+    /// Reads the chips for the current text: recent searches, then the frequent ones not already listed.
+    func refreshSuggestions() async {
+        let typed = text
+        let recent = await history.recent(matching: typed, limit: Self.suggestionLimit)
+        let chips: [SmileySearchHistoryEntry]
+        if typed.isEmpty {
+            chips = recent
+        } else {
+            let recentTexts = Set(recent.map(\.text))
+            let top = await history.top(matching: typed, limit: 10).filter { !recentTexts.contains($0.text) }
+            chips = Array((recent + top).prefix(Self.suggestionLimit))

Fixed in 543087af: the test is renamed and its comment now says what it covers, i.e. all matches show most recent first when they are under the limit. With a recent limit equal to the chip limit, a frequent match can only complete the chips when there are fewer recent matches than the limit, and then it is already among them. Testing that path separately is therefore not meaningful as the code stands.
